recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add a direct Practitioner location search parameter unless a future PA decision explicitly reintroduces location as a Practitioner search surface or defines a cross-resource chained search requirement.
issue_request: FHIR-3849 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration change request from DSTU1 asking for a search parameter so implementations could produce a list of workers at a Location.
initial_application: Commit 17d3e7f892683f3a42a65c384c3c4d7c253dd64f applied Tracker #3849 by adding a location reference search parameter on the then-current Practitioner spreadsheet. Later modeling moved role/location details from Practitioner role content into PractitionerRole.
additional_context: Practitioner and PractitionerRole are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. Current PractitionerRole defines PractitionerRole.location as Reference(Location), provides PractitionerRole-location as a reference SearchParameter with expression PractitionerRole.location, and the Practitioner narrative says role, organization, and location details are provided by PractitionerRole. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-3849 evidence that changes this interpretation.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. A direct Practitioner-location search parameter would point at no current Practitioner element and would duplicate the successor PractitionerRole search surface.
